title: How to Calculate Your Term Insurance Cover: A Practical Guide
description: Relying solely on a 10-15 times annual income rule for term insurance cover is often insufficient for comprehensive financial planning. A robust calculation m.

faq.q: What is the ideal age to buy term insurance?
faq.a: It is generally advisable to buy term insurance as early as possible, typically in your late 20s or early 30s, when you are young and healthy. Premiums are significantly lower at a younger age and remain level throughout the policy term.

faq.q: Can I increase my term insurance cover later?
faq.a: Yes, many term insurance plans offer an "increasing cover" option or allow you to purchase additional cover at significant life stages like marriage or childbirth, without fresh medical underwriting. However, this depends on the specific policy terms.

Yes, premiums paid for term insurance are eligible for deduction under Section 80C of the Income Tax Act, 1961, up to a limit of ₹1.5 lakhs. The death benefit received by nominees is also tax-exempt under Section 10(10D).

faq.q: How does inflation affect my term insurance cover?
faq.a: Inflation erodes the purchasing power of money. A cover that seems adequate today might be insufficient to meet your family's needs 10-15 years later. It's crucial to factor in an inflation rate (e.g., 6-7% annually) when projecting future expenses like education and living costs.

faq.q: Should NRIs consider term insurance from India?
faq.a: Many Non-Resident Indians (NRIs), especially those in the Gulf, choose to buy term insurance from India. This is often due to competitive premiums, a wide range of product options, and the convenience of having a policy in their home country, which is beneficial if they plan to return.

faq.q: What is the "waiver of premium" rider?
faq.a: The waiver of premium rider is an add-on benefit where all future premiums for your term insurance policy are waived if you suffer a critical illness or permanent disability, as defined in the policy document. The policy benefits continue uninterrupted, ensuring your family remains protected.
